authority: Cambridge International AS & A Level Computer Science 9618 syllabus, 2027-2029, Version 2

records.resolution: Directly distinguishes security, privacy and integrity in visible CORE teaching, practice and assessment, including cases where one property holds while another fails.
Explains why both data and the computer system require protection and rejects file encryption as a complete computer-system security control.
Covers every named Version 2 measure from stand-alone PC to network: user accounts, passwords, digital signatures, biometrics, firewall, anti-virus, anti-spyware and encryption.
Teaches virus, spyware, hackers, phishing and pharming as distinct threat mechanisms and assesses the easily confused pairs directly.
Matches controls to attack routes and states that controls restrict likelihood or impact rather than guarantee total prevention.
Separates encryption from access rights, explains how each protects data and rejects the false claim that access rights detect changes.
Covers range, format, length, presence, existence and limit checks plus check digit, including the two-bound range versus one-bound limit distinction.
Separates entry verification from transfer verification and covers visual check, double entry, parity on a byte, block parity and checksum with direct assessment.
Replaces the control-to-goal infographic so access rights prevent unauthorised actions while hash/checksum comparison, not permissions, detects change.
Replaces the biometric infographic so matching authenticates an identity claim and authorisation remains a separate access-rights decision.
Replaces the validation infographic with all seven required methods and prevents type check from substituting for an official category.
Replaces the verification infographic with separate entry and transfer methods, including byte parity, block parity and checksum.
Raises the hero-card explanation to white with sufficient selector specificity so the later academic theme cannot restore low-contrast dark text over the blue-green gradient.
